Hart's has quickly become one of my favorite spots in Brooklyn. I arrived right at opening (5:30pm) and was seated at the bar immediately. It's super convenient if you're coming off the A/C. The playlist was great and the vibe was calm and unhurried.

The food is where Hart's really shines. The roast oysters with vermouth butter and horseradish were the standout of the night, perfectly balanced with just the right amount of kick. The savoy cabbage with serrano ham and borlotti beans was homey and comforting. The clam toast with pancetta was deeply savory and something I'd come back for on its own. The seafood rice was the one dish that didn't quite land for me. Not bad, just the least memorable of the bunch.

Highly recommend

Everything was very very good. Portions: so big. The only thing I was not too fond of was the way over eggy taste of the francese sauce. Otherwise the pasta was fresh and aldente to perfection, sauce delicious and chicken in the francese was very good!
I am excited to go again and try something else! Get two or three plates and share all around!!!

text.text:
Ten Bells continues to be one of Brooklyn’s most reliable wine bars. Lively, and consistently enjoyable.

The wine list is thoughtfully curated, with an impressive range available by the glass, including draft options during happy hour at genuinely reasonable prices. I especially appreciate being able to find Spanish beers on offer (a small but distinctive touch that sets it apart) The tapas menu is extensive and well-suited for sharing, and the oysters are consistently fresh and well-priced, making them an easy go-to.

I’ve been coming here for several years and have yet to have a truly bad experience. Most recently, on Valentine’s Day weekend 2026, we walked in around 6:30 PM after a stroll through the park, no reservations, fully expecting a long wait. Despite a packed room and what appeared to be a slightly understaffed floor, we were seated without issue and still managed to catch happy hour.

Service was understandably slower given the volume, but never inattentive or unfriendly. The energy remained warm, not chaotic. Even at full capacity, the space maintains an inviting, neighborhood feel rather than tipping into frenzy.

Ten Bells isn’t about flash. It’s about good wine, solid small plates, and a dependable atmosphere. For happy hour alone, it remains one of the better values in the area and a place I’ll continue returning to.

We ordered three pastas to share… carbonara, spaghetti al limone with grilled chicken (my favorite) and rigatoni ragu. Delicious dishes! We will be back :)

I was looking for an authentic Italian experience and I found it! Handmade pasta and the BEST house sauces (lemon, cream, red - everything is uniquely delicious). Generous portions of crab and other proteins. Try the veal meatballs and mushroom bruschetta. Explore vegetarian options too!

They can sub today’s house pasta in most dishes which I love. Ask for the specials because they tend to have many off-menu options every day. Seating is somewhat intimate but never uncomfortable. The server was so attentive despite a full house on a weekend.

I spent my birthday weekend in New York, visiting from Maryland, and chose Mango Bay for my birthday dinner. I'm happy to say it exceeded all my expectations!
We started with the cocktails, a Lychee Mojito and a Grand Bay, and both were refreshing and expertly crafted. For appetizers, we ordered the Coconut Ginger Beer Mussels and Peppa Shrimps, which were packed with flavor and the perfect way to start the meal.
For our entrées, we had the Oxtail with Rice & Peas and Sweet Plantains and the Suya Ribeye Steak with Potatoes. Every dish was incredibly flavorful, well-seasoned, and absolutely delicious. You could tell a lot of care went into the preparation.
Our server was knowledgeable, friendly, and attentive throughout the evening, making the experience even more enjoyable.
Overall, Mango Bay provided an outstanding birthday dinner experience. If you're in Brooklyn and love Afro-Caribbean cuisine, I highly recommend giving this place a try. I'll definitely be back!

Very nice restaurant in a brownstone bldg with large windows, a full bar, beautiful Afrocentric art and a spiral staircase to the second floor.

The food was pricey but amazingly delicious 🤤. We had a truffle burger (8 out of 10), braised oxtails (8 out of 10), rice and beans (7 out of 10), Ras & pasta (8 out of 10) , mussels appetizer (10 out of 10) and Caesar salad (9 out of 10).

The wait staff were friendly and courteous but I thought could've been a bit more attentive as we had to actively search for our water glasses to be refilled and also seek out someone after no one came to take the drink order.

Other than that there was live music that was really nice (although a bit too loud).

I'd definitely recommend visiting this place for lunch/dinner.
